title: London Marathon receives World Athletics Award Heritage Plaque
claims: The World Athletics Heritage Plaque was announced on the anniversary of the inaugural race, 29 March 1981, recognising an outstanding contribution to the worldwide history and development of the sport.

World records have been set at the London Marathon on six occasions: once in the men's race, four times in the women's-only race and once in the women's mixed-race category, with Paula Radcliffe creating two of those moments.

Ingrid Kristiansen (Norway) and Eliud Kipchoge (Kenya) each won four men's titles; Tanni Grey-Thompson won the women's wheelchair race six times and David Weir won the men's wheelchair race eight times.
Since 1981 more than 1.2 million people have completed the London Marathon and more than £1.2 billion has been raised for charity; a record 578,000 people applied in the ballot for the 2024 event.
